title: Finite residue field points are closed in finite-type fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $x\in X$ map to $s\in S$, and let $X_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ is a finite field extension, meaning that $\kappa(x)$ is finite-dimensional as a $\kappa(s)$-vector space [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension], then the point of $X_s$ induced by $x$ is closed in $X_s$.

source.place: Tags 01TE and 01TF: Tag 01TE proves that an algebraic residue-field extension makes the point closed in its fibre; the stated finite extension is algebraic (Tag 01TF gives the converse under locally finite type).
